title: Create Mono and Flux and subscribe to them
example:
Input: Mono.just("Pravudatta"), Flux.just(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
Output: Pravudatta followed by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
hint: Use Mono for zero or one item and Flux for zero to many items. Subscribe to consume and print the values.
complexity: Time: O(n), Space: O(n) for the emitted values
interviewFollowUp: Are Mono and Flux eager or lazy, and what happens if you never subscribe?

title: Filter users aged 18 or above
example:
Input: Users (Amit, 17), (Ravi, 25), (Neha, 20)
Output: Ravi and Neha
hint: Convert the list into a Flux, filter using the age predicate, and collect the results into a list.
complexity: Time: O(n), Space: O(k) for k matching users
interviewFollowUp: What is the difference between filter() and handle() in Project Reactor?

title: Calculate product prices including 18% GST
example:
Input: Apple = 100.00, Grapes = 120.00
Output: Apple = 118.00, Grapes = 141.60
hint: Use map() to transform each product into a new product with the same name and an updated BigDecimal price.
complexity: Time: O(n), Space: O(n) for the returned list
interviewFollowUp: Why is map() appropriate here, and why should monetary calculations use BigDecimal rather than double?

title: Fetch a user and then fetch their orders
example:
Input: User ID = U101
Output: [U101-Order1, U101-Order2]
hint: Start with Mono<User> and use flatMapMany() when the next operation returns Flux<Order>. The orders can come from an asynchronous service.
complexity: Time: O(n) for n emitted orders, excluding service latency; Space: O(n) when collecting all orders
interviewFollowUp: When would you use flatMap(), flatMapMany(), or concatMap()?

title: Remove duplicate email addresses
example:
Input: [a@test.com, b@test.com, a@test.com, c@test.com]
Output: [a@test.com, b@test.com, c@test.com]
hint: Use distinct() to remove duplicate elements while preserving first-occurrence order for this sequence.
complexity: Expected time: O(n), Space: O(u) for u unique elements
interviewFollowUp: How does distinct() determine equality for custom objects, and how does it differ from distinctUntilChanged()?

title: Combine user profile and account details
example:
Input: Profile = Ravi, Account = A101/SAVINGS
Output: UserAccountResponse(Ravi, A101, SAVINGS)
hint: Use Mono.zip() to combine the independent publishers, then map the tuple into a response DTO.
complexity: Time: O(1) for DTO mapping, excluding upstream work; Space: O(1) for the response
interviewFollowUp: What happens if one publisher errors or completes empty before Mono.zip() can produce a result?

title: Compose independent service calls sequentially and concurrently
example:
Input: Profile service and Orders service each take about 500 ms
Output: Both results combined; concurrent composition can take approximately 500 ms plus overhead instead of approximately 1000 ms
hint: Use flatMap() for dependent sequential operations. For independent publishers, Mono.zip() can combine results concurrently when their underlying work supports overlapping execution.
complexity: Two independent 500 ms delayed operations: approximately 1000 ms sequential versus 500 ms when overlapped, plus overhead
interviewFollowUp: Does Mono.zip() automatically make blocking operations concurrent, and how would you safely integrate blocking legacy calls?

title: Return a fallback when a product service fails
example:
Input: Product API emits an error
Output: Default product
hint: Use onErrorResume() when recovery requires an alternate publisher, or onErrorReturn() for a fixed fallback value.
complexity: Time: O(1) for the fixed fallback, excluding upstream work; Space: O(1)
interviewFollowUp: What is the difference between onErrorResume(), onErrorReturn(), and doOnError()?

title: Retry a failed service request up to two times
example:
Input: Service fails twice and succeeds on the third attempt
Output: Request successful; Attempts: 3
hint: Use Mono.fromCallable() to simulate the request and Retry.max(2) to allow two retries after the initial attempt.
complexity: Time: O(a) service attempts plus their latency, where a is at most 3; Space: O(1)
interviewFollowUp: How would you add exponential backoff, retry only transient errors, and avoid retrying non-idempotent operations unsafely?

title: Apply a timeout to an unresponsive service
example:
Input: Service emits no response within two seconds
Output: Fallback response
hint: Use timeout() to produce a timeout error, then onErrorReturn() to emit a fallback value.
complexity: Time: Up to approximately 2 seconds before fallback, plus scheduling overhead; Space: O(1)
interviewFollowUp: Does timeout() cancel the upstream subscription, and how is a timeout different from a retry policy?
